question: Should OpenClaw accept an ACP-specific gateway-owned node runtime and command surface now, or pause it until the node command streaming/storage/security architecture is settled?
rationale: The PR changes durable runtime state and the gateway-node trust boundary; automation can identify blockers, but maintainers must decide whether this ACP-specific runtime shape is the intended product and security direction.

options.title: Pause until blockers and proof are resolved
options.body: Require the storage, delivery, reconnect, idempotency, conflict, and real-behavior proof blockers to be fixed before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Sponsor the ACP-specific runtime shape
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the product/security direction, then still require the concrete P1 fixes and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Replace with a narrower architecture path
options.body: Close or supersede this branch if the intended direction is a generic long-running node command primitive plus a smaller ACP integration later.

recommendation.title: Pause until blockers and proof are resolved
recommendation.body: Require the storage, delivery, reconnect, idempotency, conflict, and real-behavior proof blockers to be fixed before reconsidering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history makes steipete the strongest available owner for ACP runtime, gateway/node, and auto-reply architecture decisions across the touched surfaces.
